messages:
Maya (PM): Quick alignment thread: aiming to finalize Dedicated pool SKUs, default autoscale behavior, and GA launch guardrails. Please call out hard blockers by EOD.
Alex (Eng): High level thought: make predictable commit pricing the path of least surprise. Keep burst as an opt-in paid feature rather than default.
Rajat (Infra): Implementation tradeoff: three SKU shapes seems doable, but regional standby/prewarm increases infra complexity (cross-az networking, double allocation). Need timeline impact.
Lina (CS): Field feedback: customers ask for 'guaranteed response window' and explicit billing for burst usage. They also want an escape hatch when latency spikes.
Omar (SRE): Operational constraints: eviction semantics must be explicit per SKU (soft drain vs immediate preempt). Suggest standardized incident playbooks mapped to each eviction mode.
Priya (Finance): Pricing needs: we need commit tiers and a way to meter short burst windows (e.g., 5/10/15 min buckets) so customers can forecast costs. Also require baseline utilization scenarios to model margins.
Maya (PM): Draft SKU sketches: 
```
- Core-Reserve: small commit (40 rps), no included prewarm, optional pay-per-minute prewarm add-on
- Performance-Reserve: mid commit (250 rps), includes light prewarm (weights pinned), 99p latency target, 10m soft burst credits
- Enterprise-Reserve: large commit (1.2k rps), regional standby + full warm nodes, SLA-backed latency + priority support
```
Alex (Eng): Note on 'light prewarm': we can leave model weights pinned but lazily init kernels/processes. It's a middle ground that saves cost but still reduces some cold-tail. Full warm costs more but gives the tightest p99.
Rajat (Infra): Rough schedule: light prewarm is ~2 sprints to prototype (pin + lazy init), full warm + regional standby is ~4-5 sprints (runtime changes + cross-region sync).
Lina (CS): Customers with strict latency SLAs will pay for full warm. Recommend we expose a clear add-on pricing sheet for customers to opt into full warm or standby.
Omar (SRE): Autoscaling defaults proposal: 
```
- scale_up: trigger when pending queue > 40ms for 60s OR node cpu > 75% for 30s
- scale_down: remove nodes after sustained idle for 12m AND cpu < 25%
- burst_window: allow 2x capacity for up to 10m, then step down over 5m to baseline with best-effort routing
```
Alex (Eng): Also propose a configurable fallback chain per SKU: primary -> quantized variant -> distilled model. Fallback toggles must be rollable via canary.
Maya (PM): GA acceptance criteria (initial):
- 3 pilots (one per SKU) complete verification of SLA and billing clarity
- Billing metering for burst windows implemented and documented
- Eviction & rollback playbooks published; oncall trained
- Pricing approved by Finance and a publicly consumable pricing sheet ready
Priya (Finance): I'll run revenue/cost sims once we have expected utilization bands (idle/normal/peak) for each SKU. Please provide by Monday.
Lina (CS): I'll recruit pilots: indie gaming company for Core-Reserve, mid-market analytics for Performance-Reserve, regulated payments company for Enterprise-Reserve. They accept SOW with defined burst & eviction terms.
Alex (Eng): Open technical questions for RFC: 1) default fallback order and per-tenant overrides, 2) cache sharing policy across tenants in same pool, 3) burst metering resolution (minute vs 10s), 4) autoscale hysteresis tuning. I'll prepare RFC.
Rajat (Infra): Created infra task via deploy-bot: INFRA-2109 "prewarm modes + SKU plumbing" assigned to infra squad.
deploy-bot: Task INFRA-2109 created and assigned to @Rajat.
Omar (SRE): Add observability requirements: per-tenant latency percentiles, tokenized cost attribution, active prewarm counts, and burst window timelines. These must be visible in console for GA.
Maya (PM): Observability is required for GA. Add to acceptance checklist.
Priya (Finance): Also confirm how we invoice burst: aggregated per billing window or per-minute accurate? Need definition to finalize pricing.
Lina (CS): For pilot SOWs we'll define burst as 'billing windows of N minutes where capacity > baseline' and set explicit thresholds.
Alex (Eng): I'll put together the RFC with proposed defaults and fallback mechanics; target is next Wed. After RFC we lock SKUs and sequence work.
Maya (PM): Action list: Alex -> RFC, Rajat -> infra epic (done), Lina -> pilots & SOWs, Priya -> pricing sims, Omar -> runbook & observability dashboard spec. Post updates here as things land. Thanks everyone :rocket:
